failures.title: Subaru FB20 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails
failures.goodYearsLine: The FB20 improved significantly over its production run. FB20D (2017+) with direct injection is more fuel-efficient but more prone to carbon buildup. Later piston ring revisions (post-2015) reduced oil consumption issues. The FB20 is generally more reliable than the EJ20, especially with the timing chain eliminating belt failure risk .

variants.title: FB20 Variants - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: INTRO: While FB20 is the family name, there are two primary variants - the earlier port-injection FB20B and the later direct-injection FB20D. The differences matter when buying a replacement. ### FB20B - 2010-2016 (port injection) - Fitted to: Subaru Impreza GJ/GP (2012-2016), Subaru XV GP (2012-2017), Subaru Forester SJ (2013-2016) - Key technical difference: Naturally aspirated, DOHC, 16-valve. Port injection (fuel injectors in the intake manifold). Compression ratio: 10.5:1. Power: 148 hp (110 kW) at 6,200 rpm, 196 Nm at 4,200 rpm. Timing chain (no belt). Single AVCS (variable valve timing on intake only). Uses conventional multi-port fuel injection. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Oil consumption is the primary issue on this variant - early engines (2012-2014) are more prone to piston ring wear. - Interchange note: Direct swap with FB20D is not possible without significant ECU and wiring changes (fuel system, injectors, high-pressure pump). Ensure the replacement matches your engine's injection type. ### FB20D - 2017-present (direct injection) - Fitted to: Subaru XV GT (2017-present), Subaru Forester SK (2018-present), Subaru Impreza (2017-present, some markets) - Key technical difference: Naturally aspirated, DOHC, 16-valve. Direct injection (fuel injectors directly in the cylinder head). Compression ratio: 12.5:1 (higher than FB20B). Power: 150 hp (110 kW) at 6,200 rpm, 194 Nm at 4,200 rpm. Dual AVCS (variable intake and exhaust valve timing). Features a high-pressure fuel pump. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Carbon buildup on intake valves is the primary issue - a known downside of direct injection. Oil consumption is less common than on FB20B. - Interchange note: Not a straight swap with FB20B - fuel system, ECU, wiring loom, and high-pressure pump differ completely. Use the correct variant for your model year. ### FB20 e-Boxer (mild hybrid) - 2018-present - Fitted to: Subaru XV e-Boxer, Subaru Forester e-Boxer - Key technical difference: FB20D with a mild hybrid system (12V lithium-ion battery and integrated starter-generator). The engine itself is identical to FB20D mechanically, but the hybrid ancillaries and ECU are different. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Same as FB20D - carbon buildup. Hybrid-specific components (battery, motor) have their own separate failure modes (not covered on this page). - Interchange note: Not a direct swap with non-hybrid FB20D without the full hybrid system. Only replace with another e-Boxer engine.

- the 1.8‑litre turbocharged boxer introduced in 2020 for the Levorg and some Japanese models. Not yet widely available in the UK, but represents the next generation of Subaru boxer engines with improved efficiency and mild‑hybrid integration.
- the 2.5‑litre naturally aspirated variant of the FB family. Used in the Subaru Outback, Forester (North America), and Legacy. The FB25 has more torque but similar fuel consumption to the FB20.

- the 2.0‑litre direct‑injection turbo used in the Subaru BRZ / Toyota GT86 and the WRX (2015+). Though displacement is the same, the FA20 is a completely different engine family - it uses a different block, has a turbo (or higher compression for the BRZ), and is not interchangeable with the FB20.

For FB20D, look for the high-pressure fuel pump on the top of the engine - a clear visual indicator of direct injection. buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement FB20 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used FB20 makes sense if you're replacing a high-mileage unit in a lower-value car (e.g., an early Impreza or XV). However, be aware of oil consumption (FB20B) and carbon buildup (FB20D). A used engine with documented service history and low mileage (under 60k) is a reasonable bet. Avoid early FB20B (2012-2014) with no oil consumption fix applied.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper FB20 recon addresses the known weak points: for FB20B, new piston rings with improved design (to solve oil consumption); for FB20D, a thorough carbon cleaning of intake valves. Both variants get new timing chain tensioner, new water pump, and new gaskets/seals. A 12-month warranty is standard. Reconditioned units are the sweet spot for most owners - you get reliability upgrades without a full rebuild.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full FB20 rebuild is justified when you own a high-value example (e.g., a well-specced Forester or XV) and want the engine to last another 150,000+ miles. For FB20B, forged pistons can be fitted to eliminate oil consumption permanently. For FB20D, a rebuild includes new valve guides and seals to reduce carbon buildup. Budget £2,800-£4,000 for a quality rebuild.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All of our vetted UK Subaru specialists offer supply-only or full supply-and-fit - nationwide delivery and recovery available, with warranties that cover both parts and labour.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The FB20 sits in mid-range Subaru models - XV values range from £6,000-£16,000; Forester £8,000-£22,000; Impreza £4,000-£12,000 depending on year and mileage. A reconditioned FB20 at £1,800-£2,800 represents 15-35% of vehicle value - generally viable. For a high-mileage (£4,000-£6,000) early Impreza or XV, a full rebuild at £4,000 may approach 60-100% of vehicle value - evaluate the car's overall condition before committing. .

items.question: How much does a Subaru FB20 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned FB20 supply-only costs £1,800-£2,800, with fitted prices from £2,600-£3,700. Used units start from £1,200 supply-only. Rebuilt engines cost £2,800-£4,000 supply-only.

items.question: What are the most common FB20 engine problems?
items.answer: The FB20 suffers from oil consumption (FB20B, especially 2012-2014), carbon buildup on intake valves (FB20D direct-injection, 2017+), and timing chain tensioner wear (100k-150k miles). Oil consumption can require piston ring replacement (£1,500-£3,000). Carbon cleaning costs £300-£600. Timing chain tensioner replacement £400-£800.
bullets: Oil consumption can require piston ring replacement (£1,500-£3,000).

items.question: Which Subaru models use the FB20 engine?
items.answer: The FB20 is fitted to the Subaru Impreza (2012-2016), Subaru XV (2012-present), and Subaru Forester (2013-present) in the UK. The FB20B is in pre-2017 models. The FB20D is in 2017+ models with direct injection. e-Boxer variants use the FB20D with mild-hybrid system.
bullets: The FB20B is in pre‑2017 models.
The FB20D is in 2017+ models with direct injection.
e‑Boxer variants use the FB20D with mild‑hybrid system.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned FB20?
items.answer: A reconditioned FB20 is the safer choice - it includes improved piston rings (for oil consumption on FB20B) and a thorough carbon clean (for FB20D), plus a 12-month warranty. Used FB20s are acceptable if low-mileage and with service history. Avoid early FB20B (2012-2014) without oil consumption fix.
bullets: Used FB20s are acceptable if low‑mileage and with service history.
Avoid early FB20B (2012-2014) without oil consumption fix.

items.question: What’s the difference between FB20 and EJ20?
items.answer: The FB20 replaces the EJ20 - it has a timing chain (no belt replacement), improved fuel economy, and lower emissions. The FB20 is also quieter and smoother, but early FB20B units suffered oil consumption, which the EJ20 didn’t have as severely. See the EJ20 page for details
bullets: The FB20 is more modern but not a direct swap into an EJ20 car.

items.question: How long does an FB20 engine last?
items.answer: With regular maintenance (oil changes every 6k miles), an FB20 can exceed 150,000 miles. Oil consumption may appear around 60k-120k miles. Carbon buildup on FB20D can be managed with regular cleaning. Timing chain tensioner may need replacement around 100k-150k miles.

Carbon buildup on FB20D can be managed with regular cleaning.
Timing chain tensioner may need replacement around 100k-150k miles.
